title: Asymptotes and limits at infinity
objective: Distinguish holes, vertical asymptotes and end behavior, and sketch a rational function.

items: A finite limiting point missing from the graph.
The separate limits as $x$ goes to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$.
A nonhorizontal line the graph approaches at an end.

blocks.alt: Rational graph with an open point at (1, negative 1), a vertical asymptote at x equals 3, and a horizontal asymptote at y equals 1.
blocks.caption: The original function $(x^2-1)/((x-1)(x-3))$ excludes both 1 and 3. The graph uses an open point at the canceled exclusion.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: A zero denominator may cancel to a hole. The sign at negative infinity can differ. Avoid replacing $\sqrt{x^2}$ with $x$ on negative inputs.

blocks.title: Written exam practice
blocks.md: State one-sided limits at poles and both end limits when relevant. For slant asymptotes, show the quotient and the vanishing remainder.

blocks.title: Curve sketching and rational asymptotes
blocks.focus: Write down the domain restrictions before sketching each branch.

blocks.title: A hole and a vertical asymptote

steps.title: Factor
steps.why: The original denominator excludes both inputs.

steps.title: Analyze finite exclusions
steps.md: At 1 the reduced limit is $-1$. At 3 the left limit is $-\infty$ and the right is $+\infty$.
steps.why: The numerator near 3 is positive and the denominator switches sign.

steps.title: Divide
steps.why: The quotient isolates the linear growth.

steps.title: Take the difference
steps.md: The remainder $5/(x-2)$ tends to 0 at both ends.
steps.why: The difference test identifies the line.
